PURPOSE. The page computes arctan(1/70) to about 63 decimals with the Gregory series. It belongs to the same project as the neighbouring pages: I. Atg 1/99 (previous page) and III. Atg 1/5 (next page).

HEADER (Gauss's notation). (1) = arctan 1 = pi/4 belongs to the Gaussian prime 1+i. (13) = (2/3) = arctan(2/3) belongs to 3+2i, of norm 13. (29) = (2/5) = arctan(2/5) belongs to 5+2i, of norm 29.
- Since 70^2+1 = 4901 = 13^2*29, we have (3+2i)^2(5+2i) = (5+12i)(5+2i) = 1+70i.
- Taking arguments: pi/2 - arctan(1/70) = 2 arctan(2/3) + arctan(2/5).
- Hence arctan(1/70) = 2(1) - 2(13) - (29) = 2(1) - 2(2/3) - (2/5).
- The leading 2(1) is the partly struck/overwritten symbol at the start of the header.
- Likewise on the previous page (1-i)(3+2i)^2(5-2i) = 99+i, so arctan(1/99) = -(1) + 2(13) - (29). On the next page (1-i)(3+2i) = 5-i, so arctan(1/5) = (1) - (13).
- [My inference] Eliminating (13) and (29) gives pi/4 = 4 arctan(1/5) - arctan(1/70) + arctan(1/99). This is a Machin-type formula, equivalent to Machin's because arctan(1/239) = arctan(1/70) - arctan(1/99). So the three values serve a high-precision computation of pi and/or of the basis angles (13), (29).

Header: as transcribed, '= 2(2/3) - (2/5)' lacks the term 2(1) (pi/2) and the minus sign on 2(2/3). The correct identity, consistent with the right-hand side 2(1) - 2(13) - (29), is arctan(1/70) = 2(1) - 2(2/3) - (2/5). This is most likely a transcription issue with the struck/overwritten symbols rather than Gauss's error.

Rows are truncated, not rounded, at the 63rd decimal; for example 1/70^3 ends ...186588 while the true continuation is ...1865889. The final digits therefore carry an accumulated truncation uncertainty of a few units in the last place.

results.what: Decomposition arctan(1/70) = pi/2 - 2 arctan(2/3) - arctan(2/5), from the Gaussian-integer factorization 1+70i = (3+2i)^2 (5+2i), with 70^2+1 = 13^2*29
results.modern_name: Arctangent relations via factorization of n^2+1 in Z[i] (Gaussian-prime basis of arctangents; Stormer theory)
results.usually_credited_to: Arctangent identities go back to Machin (1706) and Euler (1755/1779). The systematic Z[i] approach is due to Gauss, and later Stormer (1896).

results.what: Combined with arctan(1/99) and arctan(1/5) from the adjacent pages, this implies pi/4 = 4 arctan(1/5) - arctan(1/70) + arctan(1/99)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (18th c.); used by Rutherford (1841) for pi

results.what: Evaluation of arctan(1/70) to ~63 decimals by the Gregory series. Powers 1/70^n are obtained by repeated division by 4900; positive and negative terms are summed separately and then subtracted.
results.modern_name: Gregory-Leibniz arctangent series, high-precision hand computation

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine high-precision Gregory-series computation within Gauss's well-documented work on arctangent tables and Gaussian-integer arctangent relations (cf. Werke II). The page is arithmetically accurate but contains no new mathematics.
